subject: Where does Redwood process customer inference requests? (data flow & deletion)
messages:
From: Ben Lawson <ben.lawson@greenbank.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenbank.com, edo@greenbank.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency & deletion — quick clarifications

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security and procurement teams before we proceed to the commercial side:

1) For API requests routed to Redwood's hosted offering, where exactly are requests processed? We need a short description of the sequence of regions (origin → edge → inference host) and whether any intermediate hops leave the EU for customers that require EU-only processing.

2) Which subprocessors could touch request payloads (inference inputs & short-term KV cache) for EU-region customers? We need names, locations, and whether they perform persistent storage.

3) On deletion: if GreenBank submits a deletion request, what is the timeline for removing cached prefixes, KV entries, and any temporary inference artifacts? Any proof/evidence we can provide to auditors?

Appreciate a concise Q&A we can show procurement and the DPO. If helpful, you can send a short processing map and approximate retention windows.

Best,
Ben
Ben Lawson
Head of Integrations, GreenBank

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Ben Lawson <ben.lawson@greenbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency & deletion — quick clarifications

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear list. Sending a concise Q&A below and attaching a visual processing map and a table with deletion/retention commitments. Short answers first, then a compact evidence checklist you can present to Eleni / procurement.

Short Q&A (EU-region customers):
- Where requests are processed: Primary inference execution occurs in the EU region you select (Frankfurt or the new Dublin cluster); edge ingress happens at the nearest Redwood edge node which only forwards encrypted request payloads to the chosen EU inference pool. There are no planned routing hops to non-EU inference hosts for customers who opt into EU-only execution.
- Subprocessors that may receive request data:
  • Cloud infra provider (compute) — AWS (eu-central-1 / eu-west-1) or our dedicated partner pool; performs transient in-memory processing and ephemeral block storage for checkpoints. No long-term persistent indexing of request payloads.
  • Metrics & monitoring — Datadog EU tenancy; only anonymized metrics and aggregated traces are exported.
  • Artifact storage (model weights / deployment assets) — encrypted object storage in EU.
  • Optional log collection (by customer opt-in) — S3-like bucket under customer control or Redwood-managed EU bucket; if Redwood-managed, logs are stored in EU and covered by deletion commitments.

- Deletion timeline:
  • KV cache / ephemeral inference state: typically purged within 30 minutes after completion of the session; explicit deletion request triggers immediate asynchronous purge across the cluster (best-effort completion within 1 hour; confirmation log generated).
  • Prefix/prompt caching: default TTL 24 hours; can be configured to 0 for strict residency customers. Explicit deletion request will remove cached entries within 24 hours and trigger a background invalidation across edge/pop caches (proof delivered as invalidation timestamp).
  • Persistent artifacts & logs: if managed by Redwood, deletion requests remove objects per the retention table (see attached spreadsheet) — standard SLA is 30 days for full removal from active storage and 90 days to ensure removal from cold backups, with attestations on request.

Evidence checklist to share with auditors:
- Processing map (attached) showing ingress edge → EU inference pool → storage nodes.
- List of subprocessors and region assignments (we include contact points).
- Deletion confirmation receipts (we can issue a signed deletion receipt per deletion request).
- SOC2 summary and recent penetration test executive summary (available on request).

I attached: redwood_processing_map_v2.pdf and redwood-deletion-sla-and-retention-table.xlsx.

If Eleni wants a short recorded walkthrough of the map, happy to schedule — Marissa can join for infra details and Karhtik can cover policy/retention knobs.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_processing_map_v2.pdf (processing map), redwood-deletion-sla-and-retention-table.xlsx (retention windows)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Data residency & deletion — quick clarifications

Olga / Karthik — FYI: Ben forwarded the DPO's initial comments; they will want explicit subprocessors for our EU model hosting partner and whether backups ever replicate outside the EU. Notes for the response:

- Confirm final list of third-party SaaS (Datadog EU tenancy confirmed; S3 buckets in EU if customer chooses Redwood-managed).
- Capture the exact language for "no planned routing hops to non-EU inference hosts" — legal may want a slightly softer formulation: "Redwood does not route inference execution to non-EU hosts for customers who select EU-only processing; exceptions only for emergency failover with prior customer authorization."

Also, procurement will ask for a sample deletion receipt format. Karthik — can you draft a one-paragraph attestation and an example signed receipt we can attach back to GreenBank?

Marissa
VP, Sales Ops

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data residency & deletion — quick clarifications

Adding the attestation blurb (draft):

"Redwood attests that for customers who choose EU-only processing, inference execution and associated ephemeral artifacts are constrained to EU regions controlled by Redwood. Transient caches and ephemeral inference state are not persisted beyond the retention windows described; deletion requests will trigger invalidation and removal processes and Redwood will issue a signed deletion receipt confirming timestamps of removal. In the event of an emergency failover that could require routing to non-EU resources, Redwood will only do so with prior customer authorization or if required by law—such an event is recorded and reported to the customer."

I'll prepare a templated signed deletion receipt (PDF) and a short example attestation email we can attach.

Karthik
Head of Trust & Safety (Draft)

Hi Ben / Eleni — thanks for the questions and for looping your DPO in. Per internal review I attached the processing map and the retention table and included a short attestation below. Please find the next steps at the bottom (audit evidence options).

Attestation (short):
Redwood Inference confirms that for customers who select EU-only processing, both inference execution and transient artifacts (in-memory state, ephemeral KV cache, and deployment checkpoints) are executed and stored exclusively within EU regions (Frankfurt / Dublin) operated under Redwood or our EU-compute partner. Persistent logs and backups managed by Redwood are located in EU storage by default; removal requests follow the retention schedule in the attached spreadsheet. Redwood will provide a signed deletion receipt after we complete the removal process.

Audit evidence options:
- Quick: Provide processing map PDF + signed attestation (attached).
- Standard: Processing map + signed deletion receipt template + SOC2 summary (we can redact specifics).
- Full: On-site or Zoom walkthrough with infra team + copies of subprocessor contracts (requires NDA / procurement path).

If Eleni prefers, we can lock in a 30-minute walkthrough on Thursday to step through the map and confirm wording.

Next action: Ben, please confirm which evidence package you prefer and whether GreenBank wants Redwood-managed logs (we recommend customer-managed EU buckets for more control).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this part of procurement.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
